import torch
a = torch.rand((3,3), dtype=torch.float32, device='mps')

🐛 Describe the bug
I want to install PyTorch 1.7 from the source inside a conda environment. Following are the steps I am doing.
conda create --name shade_conda python=3.8
conda activate shade_conda
conda install cudatoolkit=10.2 -c pytorch
conda install cmake
conda install pyyaml
conda install numpy
conda install ninja
git clone --recursive https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch
cd $HOME/pytorch
git checkout tags/v1.7.0
git submodule sync
git submodule update --init --recursive
export CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=${CONDA_PREFIX:-"$(dirname $(which conda))/../"}
python setup.py install
Now I am getting the following error.

import torch
from torch.autograd import forward_ad
torch.random.manual_seed(49993)
def fn(input):
    inplace = False
    fn_res = torch.nn.functional.relu(input, inplace=inplace )
    return fn_res

input_tensor = torch.empty([1, 1, 16, 16], dtype=torch.float64, requires_grad=True)

nodes.bodyText:
🐛 Describe the bug
import itertools

import torch

input = [11, 17]


def f(input, dtype):
    return torch.tensor(input, dtype=dtype)


for backend, dynamic, dtype, input_type in itertools.product(
    ["eager", "inductor"],
    [False, True],
    [torch.int, torch.float],
    [list, tuple],
):

nodes.title: [Inductor][gpu][miscompile] Outputs of torch.sin abnormally change when adding an extra torch.cat node to output

nodes.bodyText:
🐛 Describe the bug
When adding an extra branch with torch.atan as output in this model:
class Model0():
    def forward(self, *args):
        min_1 = args[1].min(0)
        getattr_1 = min_1.values
        min_2 = torch.min(getattr_1, args[0])
        mean = min_2.mean(0)
        gelu = torch._C._nn.gelu(mean)
        sub = torch.sub(gelu, gelu)
        return (sub)
New:
class Model1():
    def forward(self, *args):
        min_1 = args[1].min(0)
        getattr_1 = min_1.values
        min_2 = torch.min(getattr_1, args[0])
        mean = min_2.mean(0)
        gelu = torch._C._nn.gelu(mean)
        floor = torch.floor(gelu)
        atan = torch.atan(floor)
        sub = torch.sub(gelu, gelu)
        return (atan, sub)
The output of torch.sub is expected to be the same for the same input. However, it mismatched between the 2 models.
This mismatch is seen only on cuda.
Error logs
=========================
torch_complie triggers assertion

Not equal to tolerance rtol=1, atol=0
at v4_0, v4_0
Mismatched elements: 1 / 1 (100%)
Max absolute difference: 1.11664804e-07
Max relative difference: inf
 x: array([-1.116648e-07], dtype=float32)

=========================

torch_eager does not trigger assertion
=========================

nodes.bodyText:
🐛 Describe the bug
When swapping output sequence to (div, pad_1, interpolate) in this model:
class Model0():
    def forward(self, *args):
        cat = torch.cat((args[3], args[2], args[1], args[0]), dim = 0)
        pad = torch.nn.functional.pad(cat, (0, 0, 30, 0), 'replicate')
        cos = torch.cos(pad)
        floor = torch.floor(cos)
        div = torch.div(cos, floor)
        pad_1 = torch.nn.functional.pad(cos, (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0), 'replicate')
        interpolate = torch.nn.functional.interpolate(floor, size = [1, 1], scale_factor = None, mode = 'nearest', align_corners = None, recompute_scale_factor = None, antialias = False)
        return (pad_1, interpolate, div)
The output of torch.interpolate is expected to be the same for the same input. However, it mismatched between the 2 models.
This mismatch is seen only on cuda.

at v6_0, v6_0

nodes.bodyText:
🐛 Describe the bug
When adding an extra node of torch.cat as output in this model:
class Model0():
    def forward(self, *args):
        mul = torch.mul(args[1], args[0])
        squeeze = mul.squeeze(1)
        tan = torch.tan(squeeze)
        ceil = torch.ceil(tan)
        softmax = torch.softmax(ceil, dim = 0)
        return (softmax)
New:
class Model1():
    def forward(self, *args):
        mul = torch.mul(args[1], args[0])
        cat = torch.cat((args[0], args[0], mul, mul), dim = 2)
        squeeze = mul.squeeze(1)
        tan = torch.tan(squeeze)
        ceil = torch.ceil(tan)
        softmax = torch.softmax(ceil, dim = 0)
        return (cat, softmax)

This mismatch is seen only on cuda.

🐛 Describe the bug
When swapping output sequence in this model:
class Model0():
    def forward(self, *args):
        floor = torch.floor(args[0])
        mul = torch.mul(args[1], floor)
        round_1 = torch.round(mul)
        sin = torch.sin(round_1)
        expand = sin.expand(33, 33)
        lt = torch.lt(sin, expand)
        matmul = torch.matmul(sin, expand)
        return (lt, matmul)
New:
class Model1():
    def forward(self, *args):
        floor = torch.floor(args[0])
        mul = torch.mul(args[1], floor)
        round_1 = torch.round(mul)
        sin = torch.sin(round_1)
        expand = sin.expand(33, 33)
        lt = torch.lt(sin, expand)
        matmul = torch.matmul(sin, expand)
        return (matmul, lt)

This mismatch is seen only on cuda.

🐛 Describe the bug
When swapped the input args of torch.mul from this model:
class Model0(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()

    def forward(self, args):
        interpolate = torch.nn.functional.interpolate(args, size = [8, 1], scale_factor = None, mode = 'bicubic', align_corners = None, recompute_scale_factor = None, antialias = False)
        pad = torch.nn.functional.pad(interpolate, (0, 0, 6, 0), 'reflect')
        pad_1 = torch.nn.functional.pad(pad, (0, 15), 'constant', value = 0.5)
        mul = torch.mul(pad, pad_1)
        return (mul,)
To
class Model1(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()

    def forward(self, args):
        interpolate = torch.nn.functional.interpolate(args, size = [8, 1], scale_factor = None, mode = 'bicubic', align_corners = None, recompute_scale_factor = None, antialias = False)
        pad = torch.nn.functional.pad(interpolate, (0, 0, 6, 0), 'reflect')
        pad_1 = torch.nn.functional.pad(pad, (0, 15), 'constant', value = 0.5)
        mul = torch.mul(pad_1, pad) #swapped
        return (mul,)
The output of torch.mul is expected to be the same for the same input. However, it mismatched between the 2 models. This error is seen only on cuda.
Same behavior also seen on 2.1.1+cu118
Minified repro
from numpy import testing
import torch

DEVICE='cuda'

class Model0(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()

    def forward(self, args):
        interpolate = torch.nn.functional.interpolate(args, size = [8, 1], scale_factor = None, mode = 'bicubic', align_corners = None, recompute_scale_factor = None, antialias = False)
        pad = torch.nn.functional.pad(interpolate, (0, 0, 6, 0), 'reflect')
        pad_1 = torch.nn.functional.pad(pad, (0, 15), 'constant', value = 0.5)
        mul = torch.mul(pad, pad_1)
        return (mul,)

class Model1(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()

    def forward(self, args):
        interpolate = torch.nn.functional.interpolate(args, size = [8, 1], scale_factor = None, mode = 'bicubic', align_corners = None, recompute_scale_factor = None, antialias = False)
        pad = torch.nn.functional.pad(interpolate, (0, 0, 6, 0), 'reflect')
        pad_1 = torch.nn.functional.pad(pad, (0, 15), 'constant', value = 0.5)
        mul = torch.mul(pad_1, pad)
        return (mul,)

model_1 = Model1()
model_0 = Model0()
model_0.to(DEVICE)
model_1.to(DEVICE)
input_data = torch.rand(1, 46, 1, 1).to(DEVICE)

optmodel_0 = torch.compile(model_0, fullgraph=True, backend='inductor', mode=None)
optmodel_1 = torch.compile(model_1, fullgraph=True, backend='inductor', mode=None)

model_out_0 = optmodel_0(input_data)
model_out_1 = optmodel_1(input_data)

print(f'=====version : {torch.__version__}====================')
try:
    testing.assert_allclose(model_out_0[0].detach().cpu().numpy(), model_out_1[0].detach().cpu().numpy(), rtol=1)
    print("torch_complie does not trigger assertion")
except AssertionError as e:
    print("torch_complie triggers assertion")
    print(e)
print('=========================')

print(f'=====version : {torch.__version__}====================')
try:
    testing.assert_allclose(model_out_0[0].detach().cpu().numpy(), model_out_1[0].detach().cpu().numpy(), rtol=1)
    print("torch_eager does not trigger assertion")
except AssertionError as e:
    print("torch_eager triggers assertion")
    print(e)

🐛 Describe the bug

import logging
import torch

class MyBackend(torch._TorchCompileInductorWrapper):

    def __init__(self, mode):
        super().__init__(mode, None, False)

    def __call__(self, model_, inputs_):
        logging.info("MyBackend called")

        return super().__call__(model_, inputs_)

if __name__ == "__main__":
  logging.basicConfig(format='%(asctime)s %(filename)s %(levelname)s:%(message)s', level=logging.DEBUG)

  model = torch.compile(torch.nn.Linear(10, 10).cuda(), backend=MyBackend("default"))
  inp = torch.rand(10, 10).cuda()
  model(inp).sum().backward()

dist.all_gather_into_tensor(

            )

nodes.title: `torch.linalg.ldl_solve` segfault

nodes.bodyText:
🐛 Describe the bug
I have observed that when using torch.compile to optimize a model, the performance significantly degrades during inference under torch.inference_mode . In fact, it is even worse than the performance of the non-optimized model. However, when I place the compilation process within the context of torch.inference_mode , the performance issues are resolved.
I have posted an issue on PyTorch forum (this thread) and is advised to post it here
Here is the code to reproduce my result
import torch
from torchvision.models import resnet18
import sys
from contextlib import nullcontext

# enable inference mode when compile or benchmark?
enable_when_compile = sys.argv[1] == "true"
enable_when_benchmark = sys.argv[2] == "true"


def _benchmark(
    iters,
    f,
    context,   # with torch.inference or not
    *args,
    **kwargs,
) -> float:
    """Estimates the average time duration for a single inference call in second
    Returns:
        estimated average time duration in second for a single inference call
    """
    with context():
        f(*args, **kwargs)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    start_event = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
    end_event = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
    with context():
        start_event.record()
        for _ in range(iters):
            f(*args, **kwargs)
        end_event.record()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    elapsed_time_s = start_event.elapsed_time(end_event) * 1.0e-3
    avg_time_s = elapsed_time_s / iters
    print("Estimated average time duration: {:.6f} s".format(avg_time_s))
    return avg_time_s


class BenchmarkRunner(object):
    def __init__(self, use_inference_mode: bool):
        self.context = nullcontext if not use_inference_mode else torch.inference_mode

    def __call__(self, iters, f, *args, **kwargs) -> float:
        return _benchmark(iters, f, self.context, *args, **kwargs)


@torch.no_grad()
def run():
    input = [torch.rand(8, 3, 224, 224).to(torch.device("cuda"), dtype=torch.float16)]
    net = resnet18(pretrained=False).cuda().half()
    net.eval()
    context = nullcontext if not enable_when_compile else torch.inference_mode
    compiled = torch.compile(net, mode="reduce-overhead", backend="inductor")
    with context():
        _ = compiled(*input)

    latency_compiled = BenchmarkRunner(enable_when_benchmark)(10, compiled, *input)
    latency_torch = BenchmarkRunner(enable_when_benchmark)(10, net, *input)

    print(f"enable inference mode when compile: {enable_when_compile}")
    print(f"enable inference mode when benchmark: {enable_when_benchmark}")
    print(f"not compiled latency: {latency_torch}")
    print(f"compiled latency: {latency_compiled}, speed up: {latency_torch / latency_compiled}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    run()

Error logs
My resultI tested in torch==2.1.0+cu118 on an A10 GPU:
# 1. both are disabled, speed up 2.5X, it's great!
enable inference mode when compile: False
enable inference mode when benchmark: False
not compiled latency: 0.002047449684143066
compiled latency: 0.0008150367736816407, speed up: 2.5120948529652662

# 2.  both are enabled, speed up 2.35X, great work!
enable inference mode when compile: True
enable inference mode when benchmark: True
not compiled latency: 0.0019193056106567383
compiled latency: 0.0008156064033508301, speed up: 2.3532252846121366

# 3. enable torch.inference_mode when benchmark, disabled when compiling
# the compiled model is slower than naive torch model ! help me!
# and the naive model's latency is still ~0.002
enable inference mode when compile: False
enable inference mode when benchmark: True
not compiled latency: 0.0019556352615356445
compiled latency: 0.010692658996582031, speed up: 0.18289513040309005

# 4. disable in benchmark and enable in compiling, the result is also disappointed
enable inference mode when compile: True
enable inference mode when benchmark: False
not compiled latency: 0.0020351423263549806
compiled latency: 0.011507730865478516, speed up: 0.17685001067066186

This issue is not related to compile error, so I skip this.

nodes.bodyText:
🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch
I'm working on dynamically switching optimizer in a training script for testing their training effects on my model. However, since SGD has no default value to its lr, I'll have to manually set its default lr like the following script
param_gps = [{"params": ..., "lr": 1e-3}, {"params": ..., "lr": 1e-4}]
for optim_str in ["torch.optim.SGD", "torch.optim.Adam", "torch.optim.AdamW"]
    optim_class = import_class(optim_str )
    kwargs = {"params": param_gps}
    if optim_str == "SGD":
        kwargs["lr"] = 1e-3
    optim_instance = optim_class(**kwargs)
    ...
In most other optimizers, their lr input parameter was given a default value, whereas SGD was not.
I think it will be better to set a default lr value to 0.001 in SGD so that all optimizers' input signatures can be more alike.
My suggestion is to remove its default as required, and change it to something like 1e-3.
class SGD(Optimizer):
    def __init__(self, params, lr=1e-3, momentum=0, dampening=0,
                 weight_decay=0, nesterov=False, *, maximize: bool = False, foreach: Optional[bool] = None,
                 differentiable: bool = False):
        if lr < 0.0:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid learning rate: {lr}")
